أعلنت شركة جوجل مجموعة جديدة من مزايا الأمان والخصوصية لهواتف أندرويد، تشمل الاستعانة بنماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي Gemini لاكتشاف الرسائل الاحتيالية وتحذير المستخدمين منها، بالإضافة إلى أدوات لحماية البيانات الحساسة أثناء مشاركة الشاشة ومنع تحويل المكالمات دون علم أصحاب الهواتف.
وتستعد جوجل لإطلاق خيار أمني في تطبيق الرسائل Google Messages، يتيح تفعيل ميزة اكتشاف الاحتيال (Scam Detection)، التي تستخدم نماذج Gemini المتقدمة لتحليل نوايا المرسلين وتحديد الرسائل التي قد تصدر عن جهات خبيثة.
وأوضحت الشركة أن الميزة تستطيع رصد أساليب الاحتيال التي تعتمد على بدء محادثات تبدو عادية، قبل محاولة استدراج الضحية للحصول على معلومات شخصية.
واستشهدت بمثال لشخص يدّعي امتلاك صورة للمستلم مع كلبه، ثم يواصل المحادثة ويسأله عن اسمه بعد إبلاغه بأنه أرسل الرسالة إلى رقم خاطئ.
وأكدت جوجل أن تحليل الرسائل يجري عبر بيئة Private AI Compute، التي توفر معالجة مشفرة وآمنة للبيانات، ولا تتيح لأي جهة أخرى الوصول إليها، بما في ذلك جوجل نفسها.
وتستعين الهواتف المدعومة بنموذج Gemini Nano لتحليل الروابط داخل الرسائل والتحقق من سلامتها قبل أن يضغط المستخدم عليها.

items.t: StepFun Releases Open Weights for Step 5 Preview, Publishes Technical Blog on Its Architecture
items.d: Open weights for StepFun's Step 5 Preview are live: 600B total, 27B active, 1M context. A new technical blog explains its 92-layer design, Sparse GQA and long-horizon agent training.
items.x:
StepFun released the weights of its Step 5 Preview model on October 15, keeping the open-sourcing date it announced when the model launched in September. The release includes BF16 and FP8 checkpoints on Hugging Face and ModelScope, a technical blog describing how the model was built, and supporting open-source developer tools.
Step 5 Preview is a sparse mixture-of-experts model designed for long-horizon agent tasks. It has 600B total parameters, of which 27B are active per token, and supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens. StepFun says it performs well in coding, software engineering, professional knowledge work and finance. The company also says the model currently ranks second worldwide on OpenRouter's weekly and daily usage charts.
Developers can serve the model through an OpenAI-compatible API with vLLM or SGLang, or run offline inference with Transformers. According to the model card, the FP8 checkpoint fits on a single node of four B300 GPUs or eight H200 GPUs, while the BF16 checkpoint needs eight B300 GPUs or two eight-GPU H200 nodes. StepFun notes that the full BF16 sharded workflow for Transformers has not yet been validated end to end.
The weights are not under a standard open-source license.

Key Enhancements Training Process Multimodality Through the Tokenizer Pre-Training Post-Training Evaluation Results Evaluation Cards: Apertus ❤️ EvalEval Apertus 1.5 Reproducibility Model Availability How to Get Involved Citation Our latest release, Apertus 1.5, extends the 8B and 70B Apertus 1.0 models with image/audio understanding, an optional thinking mode, a four times longer context window, improved instruction-following, and better tool use. items.t: Mathematicians Use Shanghai AI Lab's Intern-S2 to Prove 3D Ghys Conjecture, Verified in Lean
items.d: A proof of the codimension-one case of a 1995 conjecture by Etienne Ghys was developed with Intern-S2 over many rounds of dialogue, and a Peking University team formalized it in Lean.
items.x:
Shanghai AI Laboratory says its scientific multimodal model Intern-S2 helped mathematicians prove the three-dimensional case of the Ghys conjecture, a problem in complex dynamics posed in 1995 by the French mathematician Etienne Ghys. A team at Peking University then checked the main results with the Lean theorem prover.
The paper, Codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphisms, was posted to arXiv on September 29 and revised on October 13. It lists a single author, Jiesong Zhang of KTH Royal Institute of Technology. It proves that every codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected complex manifold is biholomorphically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of a complex torus, which settles the conjecture in that case and in complex dimension three. Roughly, the conjecture says that if a space supports this kind of chaotic but perfectly regular motion, the space itself must have a rigid, crystal-like structure.
The lab's announcement credits the work to a team led by Disheng Xu, a professor at Great Bay University and visiting scholar at the lab, with Zhang, his former student, joining as a visiting scholar.

items.t: Kunlun Tech releases open-source AI game system that runs on a single RTX 5090
items.d: Kunlun Tech released Matrix-Game 4.0 on October 15, an open-source system that combines a game engine with real-time AI video rendering on a single consumer graphics card. The company says it delivers 480p gameplay at 60 frames per second…
items.x:
Kunlun Tech released Matrix-Game 4.0 on October 15, an open-source system that combines a game engine with real-time AI video rendering on a single consumer graphics card. The company says it delivers 480p gameplay at 60 frames per second on an Nvidia RTX 5090, with input-to-response latency below 150 milliseconds.
The game engine maintains the world’s state, physics and interaction rules, while a video model turns simple, low-poly frames into detailed visuals. A coding agent can translate player instructions into new game rules and prompts, enabling changes to gameplay alongside AI-generated rendering.
The release includes model weights, inference code, a browser demo and game assets for shooting and driving scenarios. The team plans to improve resolution, expand support for different game types and explore multiplayer experiences with consistent views across players. [ Skywork AI ]

items.t: Doubao Work Adds One-Click Import of Skills, Memory and Chat History From ChatGPT and Claude Code
items.d: ByteDance's Doubao Work can now import preferences, skills, connectors, memory, projects and past chats from ChatGPT, Claude Code and TRAE Work, and adds annotations and a summary sidebar.
items.x:
ByteDance's AI work assistant Doubao Work has added a data import and sync feature, letting users bring their existing setups and conversations over from other AI products instead of starting from scratch. The update was announced on October 14.
Users can import task preference instructions, skills, connectors, working memory, projects and past chat sessions with one click. Supported sources include ChatGPT, Claude Code and TRAE Work. The feature imports content that those products store locally, and the imported items are automatically filed under the matching sections in Doubao Work. Imported conversations keep their original context, so users can continue them directly without reconfiguring tools or explaining the background again.
The feature sits under a Data Import and Sync page in Settings. For sources that support it, users can also turn on automatic syncing as needed, rather than doing a one-time transfer.
The same update adds several changes to how conversations work. A Continue in New Chat option on any message carries the existing context into a fresh conversation while keeping the original thread intact for reference.

items.t: Skywork Open-Sources Matrix-Game 4.0, Pairing a Game Engine With a Real-Time Video Model
items.d: Kunlun Tech's Skywork AI released Matrix-Game 4.0 under Apache-2.0: an engine runs the rules and physics while a causal video model renders low-poly frames into detailed game visuals.
items.x:
Skywork AI, the AI unit of Kunlun Tech, released Matrix-Game 4.0 on October 15, the latest version of its open-source interactive world model series. Inference code, a browser demo and the source code of three playable games are on GitHub, with model weights and game assets on Hugging Face. The new version is licensed under Apache-2.0.
The release changes how the series approaches game worlds. Instead of asking a video model to remember the world and keep track of the rules while it generates frames, Matrix-Game 4.0 keeps gameplay, physics and player input inside an executable game engine. The engine outputs a rough low-poly view of the scene, and a causal, few-step video model turns that view into detailed visuals in a streaming fashion. The team describes the approach as putting a harness on the video model: code decides what happens, and the model decides what it looks like.
That split means state such as health, item ownership and mission progress is recorded explicitly in code, so an occasional visual glitch does not rewrite the game. In a demo reported by QbitAI, a picked-up shield absorbs damage before the player's health drops, and the game ends when health reaches zero.

Through some of these features, the company aims to provide a definition for its own and third-party agents to adhere to a brand’s design rules better while creating with AI.
The company debuted a new feature called Figma Specs, which is a markdown editor that lets users define their design language in a simple way. The document can serve as a reference for teams and agents while designing in Figma. Specs can exist as a standalone file in Figma or can co-exist within the canvas. Apart from acting as a text editor, users can reference other Figma elements, such as elements on the canvas and embed FigJam diagrams, code layers, and designs.
What’s more, teams can bring in more context about design, including design libraries, code libraries, and guidelines to manage context for the design system. Agents can also refer to this centralized system to adhere to rules.

In collaboration with OpenAI, Sullivan & Cromwell developed Agreement Analyzer, an AI tool for identifying issues in a draft agreement.
For lawyers at Sullivan & Cromwell, reviewing a draft agreement includes weighing its terms against relevant precedents, using approaches based on the Firm’s experience and being mindful of a client’s priorities. The firm’s Agreement Analyzer brings those inputs into a single review workflow, producing analysis and proposed changes that lawyers can inspect and refine.
Though AI was initially used most for repetitive, administrative tasks like drafting email responses or checking calendars, Savva finds that recent improvements in AI models’ analytical capabilities have changed its usage. “Now, we’re seeing many more opportunities for use in challenging legal tasks such as deep analysis of complex agreements,” he says.
Agreement Analyzer helps lawyers compare corresponding provisions across precedents and track how those provisions interact.
Sullivan & Cromwell partner John Savva developed Agreement Analyzer as a single-user proof of concept built with Codex.

items.t: An update on independent evaluators
items.d: To evaluate the safety of our systems, Anthropic is giving employee-like access to a team from METR, a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models, and we're in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face.
items.x:
Anthropic announces updates to embedding independent evaluators
Last month, we committed to stronger independent, third-party assessment of our models and safety practices. We also signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators. Today, we’re announcing that we’ve started to give employee-like access to a team from METR, a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models.
METR will publish the results of its risk assessments. Over the past year, we’ve worked with METR on several reviews of our Risk Reports. We’re also working with SecureBio and Accenture as evaluators, and are in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face.
As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessments. We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work. Some of it could be useful to malicious actors, or is commercially sensitive, like compute or training information.

Nearly eight years after Epic took on Steam with its own Game Store and launcher, the Fortnite maker is deploying a new tool to give it an edge over Valve: vibe coding.
In announcing the new publicly available "Preview" build of its Epic Games Launcher, Epic writes that "programming is hard. So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look." And while that might sound a little tongue-in-cheek, Epic Games Store General Manager and VP Martin Keely told PC Gamer that the team "started from scratch" and used AI as "a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack than what we had previously." The goal, Keely said, was to "look at functionality that existed [in the current Epic Games Launcher] and [say] we want to replicate that, but not the code itself."
Speaking to IGN , Keely clarified that using AI to code the new Launcher "made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we're going to have a Linux version as well."

items.t: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence

Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed.
Founded in 2024 on the basis of research done in Macquarie University in Sydney, the Australian startup deploys thousands of AI agents that masquerade as innocent victims. The agents can answer scam calls, respond to shady messages and emails, follow phishing links, and join social media groups to bait fraudsters. They pretend to be people of all stripes, sporting different ages, genders and accents, and speak various languages as they try to keep scammers engaged long enough to learn something useful.
The company says its fleet of agents has so far wasted 17 years of scammers’ time across 2.5 million conversations. More importantly for Apate’s customer base of banks, telecom companies, government agencies and utilities, the undercover agents try to get scammers to reveal things about themselves that are usually learned only after a victim has been scammed: bank accounts, crypto wallets, phone numbers, malicious websites, the brands they’re impersonating, and other details about the scams they’re running.

items.t: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
items.d: AI design tools make proteins that break bonds that are stable for hundreds of years.
items.x:
A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere, and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment.
Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases.
The basic peptide bond isn't especially interesting-looking—it's what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid.

items.t: My AI doppelganger tells me what to eat
items.d: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here. For the past 100 days…
items.x:
This week’s Optimizer delves into the concept of digital twins, a virtual version of a patient that can potentially help clinicians model medical treatments.
In return for feeding a ‘digital twin’ my metabolic data, it predicts how I’ll react to certain foods — and one day, maybe medicines.
For the past 100 days or so, my mornings have had a new rhythm. When I wake up, the first thing I have to do is feed my digital twin. It consumes my metabolic data, and its first “meal” of the day is my body composition data, sent straight from a smart scale.Once that’s logged in the app, I scoot over to the kitchen to fill an Owala with lemon water to take my medications with. That, too, gets logged in the app. On Mondays, I’ll follow that up with several calming breaths, measure my blood pressure, and offer that to the digital twin as well. Then it’s time to consider breakfast. I consult my digital twin.
My digital twin isn’t so much a robotic clone as it is an AI-powered, color-coded food database that predicts how my glucose levels will react to everything I eat. Red is not so good. Orange is so-so. Green is ideal. It’s built based on the data I feed it, as well as data collected from a continuous glucose monitor.
A bowl of protein Cheerios and milk?

items.t: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
items.d: OpenAI engineer faces 5 years and $250K fine as FBI lobs foreign spy charges.
items.x:
It took OpenAI two days to notice that a recording device was hidden in a restricted executive conference room where leadership met to discuss highly confidential information, including technical progress, government engagements, and commercial partnerships.
Only those with special clearance are supposed to access that room. But the FBI believes the recording device was planted by Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer from Saudi Arabia, who became a permanent US legal resident in 2020. In a press release Tuesday announcing his arrest, the FBI alleged that chatbot logs and CCTV footage suggested that Alfozan—who worked as an OpenAI engineer for more than a year—sought to use the device to spy on OpenAI and risked leaking trade secrets in a way that threatened national security.
To conceal the USB device, Alfozan allegedly wrapped it in toilet paper, then plugged it into the back of a conference room television. The device was likely planted on September 28, and OpenAI found it on September 30 and quickly determined that its contents were encrypted, the FBI said. Days later, on October 5, OpenAI installed a camera in that conference room, and the CCTV footage allegedly showed Alfozan attempting to retrieve the recording device that same day.

items.t: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
items.x:
Visualizing and using HiRO outputs 🤗 Models | 📄 Paper | 📓 Tutorial notebooks | 🌎 Demo
We introduce HiRO-ACEv2, the newest update to our High Resolution Output Ai2 Climate Emulator (HiRO-ACE) system. HiROv2 can reproduce even extremely rare rain, wind, and pressure events with high accuracy, while the full system can generate global 3 km climate data at about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD, a high-resolution global atmospheric model that explicitly simulates storms and other small-scale weather.
HiRO-ACE, introduced earlier in 2026, has two parts: ACE, an AI model that operates at a coarser 100 km resolution, and HiRO, a model that sharpens those coarse outputs into fine 3 km detail. The biggest change in HiRO-ACEv2 is the new downscaling model, HiROv2, which can now 1) predict several high-resolution fields at once instead of just rainfall, so it can capture a much wider range of extreme weather, and 2) has improved skill in predicting extreme events.
Our main focus with HiRO-ACEv2 was to simulate extreme events well. Changes to how we train HiROv2 improved its ability to reproduce the most intense rain, wind, and pressure values.

Streaming platform Deezer remains steadfast in its intent to help users avoid listening to AI-generated music: The company on Tuesday said it is working on a new toggle that lets users filter out AI-generated music uploaded to its platform. The feature is expected to be available before the end of the year.
Deezer said turning on the toggle will stop you from seeing AI-generated tracks, albums, and related artists in search results.
“We’ve seen clear user demand for the ability to filter out AI-generated music, and we are now giving everyone the option to remove this content completely from their streaming experience on Deezer, and focus only on human creators and creations, if they wish,” Deezer CEO Alexis Lanternier said in a statement.
He added that the explosion of AI music on the platform was one of the catalysts for the toggle-based features. The company cited a survey from last year, which noted that around 45% of Deezer customers wanted a way to remove AI music from their feeds.
Deezer added AI-detection tooling last year and has been reporting on the number of tracks being uploaded to the platform ever since.

items.t: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
items.d: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
items.x:
AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet-of-things devices and is more resistant to takedown.
By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results do raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms.
Anthropic further warned not only about the new potential malware, but also that it could be difficult to stop. In its blog post, it wrote that “a replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own.”

See how Amp pushes the frontier of what agents can do with GPT-6 Astra, Ultrafast, GPT-Live-1, and Sign in with ChatGPT.
Amp⁠(opens in a new window) is building a frontier AI agent that helps developers turn ambitious ideas into working software. For Quinn Slack, Amp’s CEO, each improvement in the models is an opportunity to expand what the agent can do, from helping developers decide what to build to writing code and designing pages.
Amp chooses and recommends models based on what works best for its users, and OpenAI models account for the majority of tokens used in Amp. Quinn shares, “OpenAI is very transparent, and when there are safeguards applied, users know and they understand. That makes it really easy to use OpenAI models. You can do all of your work in Amp with OpenAI models and be really happy.”
As builders give agents more work, token costs can become a constraint. Quinn describes some Amp users consuming 10 billion tokens a week. He believes that if people watch every increment of usage, it might hold them back from finding out what an agent is capable of.
To help alleviate that, Amp launched its Sign in with ChatGPT integration.

items.t: SentinelOne cuts malware analysis from weeks to hours
items.d: With OpenAI Daybreak, SentinelOne cuts weeks of malware analysis to hours, creating capacity to investigate more threats.
items.x:
With OpenAI Daybreak, SentinelOne cuts weeks of malware analysis to hours, creating capacity to investigate more threats.
Reverse engineering a sophisticated piece of malware can take a top security researcher four to six weeks. It’s painstaking work where researchers pull apart software to understand how it behaves, often retracing their steps as they uncover new information. Gregor Stewart, Chief AI Officer at SentinelOne, says OpenAI Daybreak can now produce human-level reverse-engineering output in roughly eight hours.
By reducing the time needed for deep analysis, OpenAI gives SentinelOne’s researchers room to investigate more malware and connect findings across samples. That wider view often reveals relationships that isolated investigations might miss. Stewart describes the opportunity as “a kind of intelligence that we were never able to afford before.”
Daybreak gives defenders access to OpenAI models for cybersecurity work. SentinelOne uses these capabilities to reverse engineer malware, examining software to understand how it behaves. Faster analysis gives its researchers more capacity to investigate additional samples.
Stewart emphasizes that his team remains responsible for the outcome. “The only thing that can’t be automated is accountability,” he says.

items.t: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
items.d: Attack method exposes flaws in OpenAI, Google safeguards against AI nudes.
items.x:
Safety researchers continue to warn that a large volume of AI-generated explicit content is spreading unchecked, while regulators do little to meaningfully stop it.
This non-consensual content is commonly shared in text and direct messages or stored in private clouds where it’s less likely to be detected or reported, a Google co-authored study of Internet users across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom found this July. That’s why the “most critical intervention point” remains at the source: the harmful AI tools used to make the fake sexual images, Google researchers concluded.
Yet red-teaming in recent months suggests that as some of the leading AI image generators from Google and OpenAI become more capable, they may be getting worse at blocking explicit outputs.

As manufacturers across industries strive to reduce their reliance on Chinese suppliers, Indian startup Scimplify has raised $25 million to expand its AI-powered approach to producing specialty chemicals and critical materials, with semiconductors, defense and energy emerging as key growth markets.
The all-equity strategic round was led by Hitachi Ventures, with customers Henkel and Teknor Apex joining as new investors. Existing backers Accel India, Bertelsmann India Investments, Omnivore, and 3one4 Capital also participated. The round values the Bengaluru-based startup at $250 million after the investment, according to a person familiar with the transaction, up from $150 million after a $40 million Series B round in March 2025. The latest investment brings Scimplify’s total equity funding to $80 million, the startup said, though it declined to disclose its valuation.
The growing adoption of AI and advanced computational tools has accelerated materials discovery and research. However, turning promising chemistry into commercially available products at scale remains a slow and complex process.

items.t: Dobot Launches VEGA 7, a Seven-Axis Force-Controlled Arm for Embodied AI With 50,000-Hour MTBF
items.d: Dobot's VEGA 7 has torque sensors and brakes in every joint, 0.15N force control accuracy, a 7kg payload and 725mm reach, aimed at wheeled dual-arm robots and embodied AI work.
items.x:
Dobot has launched DOBOT VEGA 7, a seven-axis force-controlled robotic arm designed from the start for embodied AI. The company unveiled it at a product event at the China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, positioning it for wheeled dual-arm robots, mobile manipulation in industrial settings and embodied AI development.
Dobot's main pitch is durability. The company says VEGA 7 has a mean time between failures of 50,000 hours. Every joint has an electromagnetic brake as standard, and in an unexpected power loss the arm can hold its posture and brake within 18 milliseconds. It is rated IP54 for dust and water resistance.
Every joint also carries a torque sensor, which supports contact sensing, compliant control, collision detection and hand-guided teaching. Dobot lists force control accuracy of 0.15N or better, torque control accuracy of 0.05N·m or better and force control resolution of 0.01N·m or better. The company says this makes the arm a development and validation platform for precise plugging and unplugging, small-part assembly and dual-arm coordination.
The core specifications are a rated payload of 7kg, a working radius of 725mm and repeatability of ±0.03mm.

items.t: PHANES AI Launches SeePhys Hub, a Wearable Kit That Records Vision, Touch and Full-Body Motion
items.d: PHANES AI's SeePhys Hub pairs a four-camera headband with wrist, waist and leg trackers and tactile gloves, capturing human motion and touch data for training robots.
items.x:
PHANES AI has released SeePhys Hub, a whole-body, multimodal data capture system meant to turn everyday human activity into training data for robots. QbitAI reported that the October 14 launch was a joint release with Tinno Mobile, which contributed experience in cost control, supply chain and quality assurance, while PHANES AI focused on product design and algorithms.
The kit consists of a four-camera headband, two wrist bands, three motion trackers worn on the waist and lower legs, and a pair of tactile gloves. Together they record first-person vision with 360-degree coverage, hand pose and high-density touch, and whole-body pose and force.
The company's argument is that egocentric, or Ego, data from head-mounted cameras has become a key source for robot learning because it scales easily, but it misses much of what the body is doing. A camera at eye level sees the hands, yet often not the elbows or legs, and it records nothing about how hard the hands press on an object. Tasks that require walking, bending and two-handed coordination need that missing information.
SeePhys Hub uses a sparse-node approach. The three trackers combine IMU motion signals with UWB ranging between nodes, and algorithms fuse them with head and wrist vision to estimate full-body pose.

items.t: Doubao Phone Assistant Opens Screen Automation to Third-Party Apps as 151 Apps Opt Out
items.d: ByteDance's Doubao phone assistant ended the 30-day notice period for its SAEP protocol and will gradually allow AI screen automation in third-party apps that have not opted out.
items.x:
ByteDance's Doubao phone assistant said on October 14 that the 30-day public notice period for its Screen Automation Execution Protocol, or SAEP, has ended, and that it will now gradually open screen automation for third-party apps. Under the rules, apps whose developers have not declared a refusal will become available for the assistant's AI agent to operate on users' behalf.
The opt-out does not close with the notice period. Developers can still submit a refusal at any time, and the assistant said it will promptly switch off the related operations once it receives one. Apps that have already declared a refusal will not be operated by the agent.
Alongside the announcement, the assistant published its current list of apps that have refused and said the list will be updated regularly. According to a count by National Business Daily, it covers 151 apps, including 65 apps in the Tencent ecosystem such as WeChat, QQ and Honor of Kings, and 23 apps in the Alibaba ecosystem such as Taobao, Qwen and Alipay.

Nvidia’s share of China’s data-center AI accelerator market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, while Huawei reached 28%, according to an IDC report seen by Reuters. US export restrictions constrained Nvidia’s supplies as Chinese chipmakers expanded shipments.
Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China between January and June, down 44% from a year earlier. Huawei shipped 572,000, compared with more than 300,000 in the same period last year. The chips are used to train AI models and run inference.
Alibaba’s T-Head accounted for 7% of shipments, followed by Cambricon at 5%, Kunlunxin at 4% and Hygon at 3%. Nine of the 11 Chinese suppliers tracked by IDC increased shipments during the period. [ Reuters ]

items.t: How Third Moment Research runs 10,000 agents for 36+ hours
items.d: With GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, Codex, and Daybreak for cybersecurity, this AI lab builds agents that focus for days and improve with use.
items.x:
With GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, Codex, and Daybreak for cybersecurity, this AI lab builds agents that focus for days and improve with use.
With GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol, Codex, and Daybreak for cybersecurity, this AI lab builds agents that focus for days and improve with use.
Every company has its own workflows, tools, edge cases, and definitions of success. ⁠(opens in a new window)Third Moment Research⁠(opens in a new window) believes the best agents should be really good at that specific work and should improve their capabilities the more they’re used.
The company is building a self-improving AI system around that idea, using OpenAI’s latest models to understand agent behavior, identify recurring weaknesses, and automatically create thousands of synthetic scenarios around those problems. The team uses those scenarios to improve agents, repeating the process as new issues emerge.
Codex, GPT‑6 Astra, GPT‑6 Sol, and GPT‑6.1 Sol support the system’s research and computational work, enabling Third Moment to run 10,000 agents at once on investigations lasting 36-48 hours. The company also uses Daybreak to test the security of the environments where agents work.
One of Third Moment’s early applications is in the field of quantitative finance given the clear measure of success.

items.t: MagicLab's EchoPolicy-0 Tops AI2's MolmoSpaces Combined Board With a 75.4% Manipulation Success Rate
items.d: MagicLab says its VLM agent framework EchoPolicy-0 averaged 75.4% across four MolmoSpaces tasks, and AI2's published leaderboard data lists it first. Its MagicBrain hit 94.4% on pick.
items.x:
MagicLab says its VLM agent framework for general robot manipulation, EchoPolicy-0, has taken first place on the MolmoSpaces Combined leaderboard run by the Allen Institute for AI (AI2), with an equal-weighted average success rate of 75.4% across all four v1 manipulation tasks. MolmoSpaces is a zero-shot embodied AI benchmark built on more than 230,000 indoor environments and about 130,000 object assets.
Pandaily checked the claim against the data AI2 publishes for its leaderboard. EchoPolicy-0 is listed under MagicLab, paired with Gemini-3.8-Flash as the vision-language model and evaluated on a Franka arm, in all four tasks: Pick, Pick and Place, Open and Close. Averaging the four task success rates in that data gives about 75.5%, consistent with the company's 75.4% figure after rounding, and the highest among entries that cover all four tasks.
EchoPolicy-0 links a vision-language model, geometric manipulation tools and a general action policy into one closed loop of observing, understanding the goal, choosing a skill, acting and checking the result. When an action falls short, the framework can continue, retry, replan or roll back.

items.t: Hello Inc.'s Robotaxi Unit Releases HelloWorld, a World Model That Builds Driving Scenes on Demand
items.d: HelloWorld, a generative driving world model from Hello Inc.'s robotaxi team, creates multi-view camera video and lidar data from edited layouts or plain-language prompts for testing.
items.x:
Hello Inc.'s robotaxi business has released HelloWorld, a generative driving world model designed to build driving data on demand and to test driving policies interactively. The team announced the model on October 12 and has published a paper on arXiv along with a project page.
HelloWorld brings together scene control, continuous generation, multi-sensor observation and efficient inference. Engineers can edit vehicles, pedestrians and their trajectories directly, and the model generates matching multi-view camera video together with lidar observations. Examples include inserting a pedestrian crossing the road, changing the route of the car ahead, or switching between rain, snow, day and night.
The model also accepts plain-language descriptions as a second way to build scenes. A user describes the situation they want, and an application pipeline turns it into the conditions the model needs. Construction zones, dense traffic, pedestrians crossing, fog and different lighting can all be used to steer what is generated.
The goal is to fill gaps in real-world data. Long-tail situations, such as rare hazards or unusual combinations of weather and traffic, are hard to capture enough of through road collection alone.

items.t: Tsinghua's SRHarness Helps AI Agents Find Formulas, While MechBench Tests Whether They Grasp Why
items.d: Tsinghua researchers released SRHarness, an open-source runtime for agentic symbolic regression, and MechBench, a benchmark that tests whether AI can recover the mechanisms behind formulas.
items.x:
Researchers at the Data Science and Intelligence Lab in Tsinghua University's Department of Electronic Engineering have released two linked pieces of AI for Science work: SRHarness, a runtime framework for agentic symbolic regression, and MechBench, a benchmark that asks whether AI can recover the mechanisms behind a formula rather than only the formula itself.
The team frames the work with a historical example. Kepler derived the laws of planetary motion from observations, describing how planets move; Newton's mechanics explained why. Large language models and scientific agents can now analyze data, call tools and iterate on hypotheses, so the researchers set out to test both steps.
SRHarness does not prescribe a search strategy. Instead it turns the runtime that agents rely on into reusable infrastructure with three parts: reusable scientific actions that wrap analysis, fitting, search and evaluation tools behind one interface; persistent scientific state that stores candidate formulas and their evidence outside the chat context; and trajectory lifecycle management that handles continuing, branching, restarting and stopping long searches.

items.t: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
items.d: Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.
items.x:
Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.
The collaboration delivers an on-device scam detection model that helps protect citizens without compromising privacy.
Scams make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019. At the same time, scam tactics have shifted from simple phishing to complex social engineering, whereby attackers manipulate victims with convincing conversations before requesting money. Such scams now account for up to 80% of all losses.
To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government. This has allowed us to deliver an on-device scam detection model - optimized to run on typical smartphones in Singapore - to tackle an urgent safety challenge while preserving citizens' privacy.
Generic models often struggle with localised deception techniques, making scam detection harder. To address this, Google DeepMind's lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations.

items.t: The EU’s next chapter in AI is agentic
items.d: New analysis shows how agentic AI adoption is growing across EU enterprises and small businesses—and where deeper use could unlock more value.
items.x:
New analysis shows how agentic AI adoption is growing across EU enterprises and small businesses—and where deeper use could unlock more value.
Across the EU, businesses are expanding how they use AI through agentic tools. People are moving beyond asking questions to using agents to carry out tasks from planning through completion. Our latest report from OpenAI Economic Research examines how agentic use is growing across enterprises and small businesses, focusing on differences in usage intensity and the kinds of work people do with ChatGPT.
We have found that, among ChatGPT Enterprise customers, agentic use already represents a substantial share of activity⁠. In our EU sample, Codex and ChatGPT Work now account for more than half of output tokens.
This analysis defines small or medium businesses as businesses with 200 or fewer associated users.
The agentic shift extends to small and medium businesses. Since May 2026, weekly active users of Codex and ChatGPT Work among EU small and medium businesses grew more than eightfold, with growth across every member state.
But we also found that the EU’s adoption of agentic AI is far from uniform.

items.t: Preparing for the 2026 US midterms
items.d: Earlier this year, we shared an update on our election safeguards. Here, we outline how we’ve continued to strengthen these safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms.
items.x:
Earlier this year, we shared an update on our election safeguards. Here, we outline how we’ve continued to strengthen these safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms.
Below, we outline how we’ve built on that work and continued to strengthen our election safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms.
Our goal is for Claude to be a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. That starts with understanding how people actually use Claude in these contexts. To do this, we used Anthropic Insights to develop a new analysis of 250,000 conversations over the course of a recent one-week period.1
Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app. This includes people turning to Claude to follow the news, conduct academic or professional research on public policy, learn about candidates, and navigate government services. About 0.51% of all conversations are specifically about elections or voting. As we get closer to Election Day, we expect the share of political and election-related queries to increase.
This sample suggests people rarely ask Claude who or what to vote for.

items.t: Agent observability on the Claude Platform
items.d: Announcing OpenTelemetry traces from Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and Claude SDKs on the Claude Platform.
items.x:
Announcing OpenTelemetry traces from Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and Claude SDKs on the Claude Platform.
You can now send OpenTelemetry (OTel) traces from Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and Claude SDKs to any OTel tool, and follow each step your agents take. If you already send Claude Code or Cowork traces to your observability tool, the agents you build on the Claude Platform can also show up in the same place.
Trusting an agent with more access starts with tracing its model calls, tool use, and MCP server calls. Review its traces, then widen its access as it proves reliable.
Add a destination in the Claude Console, and every agent turn, model call, and tool use arrives in your observability tool as a standard OpenTelemetry trace, with latency, tokens, and IDs.
Claude traces follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, so data from Claude and other providers works in the same tools and dashboards.
Claude traces also work with any other OpenTelemetry tool that accepts a standard OTLP endpoint.
OpenTelemetry traces on the Claude Platform is available in public beta.

اعتقلت السلطات الأمريكية مهندسًا سابقًا في شركة OpenAI، بعد اتهامه بزرع جهاز تسجيل متطور داخل أحد مكاتب الشركة.
وحددت وزارة العدل الأمريكية هوية المتهم، وهو يُدعى عبد الرحمن الفوزان، وهو مواطن سعودي يبلغ من العمر 35 عامًا، ووجهت إليه تهمة استخدام جهاز لاعتراض الاتصالات الشفهية أو محاولة استخدامه لهذا الغرض، وفقًا لبيان رسمي صادر عن الوزارة.
واكتشفت OpenAI جهاز التسجيل موصولًا بمنفذ USB في تلفاز داخل غرفة اجتماعات مخصصة للإدارة التنفيذية، تُناقش فيها معلومات شديدة السرية تتعلق بالجوانب التقنية والتجارية والإستراتيجية للشركة.
وأوضحت الشركة أنها استعانت بنماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي التابعة لها لفهم طبيعة الجهاز وتحديد مصدره، مشيرةً إلى أنها توصلت إلى أن أحد الموظفين زرعه قبل اكتشافه بأيام.
ووفقًا لوزارة العدل الأمريكية، فقد كان الجهاز مغطى بورق المرحاض، ويُعتقد أنه وُضع في مكانه في 28 سبتمبر تقريبًا، كما كانت محتوياته مشفرة.
وأفادت الوزارة بأن المتهم لم يكن مخولًا بدخول غرفة الاجتماعات، لكن تسجيلات كاميرات المراقبة أظهرت وجوده بالقرب منها في تواريخ متعددة قبل اكتشاف الجهاز.
وأضاف الادعاء الفيدرالي أن التسجيلات أظهرت المتهم وهو ينظر خلف التلفاز الذي عُثر على جهاز التسجيل بداخله.

items.t: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
items.d: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
items.x:
Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said on stage. “We consider cochlear implants, retinal prostheses, motor prostheses, these are all different types of BCIs.”
Hodak outlined a vision in which BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications, rather than simply being a way to control computers.

items.t: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
items.d: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.
items.x:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.
Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman believes we’re nearing a future where everyone will have an AI appliance in their own home.
Speaking on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Tuesday, the chipmaker executive answered a question about what would need to happen for AI to become a home appliance, saying, “Actually, I don’t think that’s very far away.”
He pointed to the advances in consumer AI agents, like Meta’s Muse and Instinct, the startup now valued at $10 billion, as examples of how AI is finding its footing with everyday users.
As for home AI? He predicts that we’ll have personal AI assistants that run locally.
“Just like your cell phone, they’ll do some work on device and some work going back to the cloud,” Feldman explained. “But I think they will get to know you very well, and you will have a security perimeter around them. And they will certainly have access to credit cards and be able to buy things for you,” he continued.

items.t: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
items.d: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.
items.x:
Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.
In most factories, automation is fixed: robots and machines are programmed for one specific task and product. Changing a line means reprogramming and physical retooling, or swapping out equipment, which can take weeks or months. San Francisco-based Industrial Next says it’s changing that.
The startup, which presented today on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, builds AI-driven, self-contained robotic stations powered by proprietary foundation models that connect vision, task context and motion. The company says this lets a production line be retooled in minutes rather than weeks without traditional programming. The goal is to let manufacturers automate complex and delicate tasks that traditionally require human labor.
The company announced on stage that it’s partnering with BMW Group Technology Office to evaluate Industrial Next’s AI-powered dexterous manipulation for manufacturing.
Industrial Next was founded in 2021 by Lukas Pankau and Allen Pan, both of whom previously worked at Tesla. Pankau served as a lead electrical architect at Tesla before moving on to Waymo.

items.t: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
items.d: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.
items.x:
Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.
Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman thinks the AI doomer narrative isn’t doing the industry any favors. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI chipmaker exec quipped that “some of the leaders in the AI world maybe shouldn’t be allowed to talk in public.”
He’s referencing the negativity now spreading around the dangers of AI, from models breaking containment to AI insiders debating the percentage chance that AI may kill all of humanity by the end of the decade. The argument has become so mainstream that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was recently parodied in a skit on Saturday Night Live, where the fictional character summed up the discourse, saying, “We do not condone what we are doing.”
Feldman, however, thinks the promise and potential that go hand-in-hand with AI developments are getting overlooked.

items.t: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
items.d: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.
items.x:
A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.
A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July.
Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device.
These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations andrecords showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components.
The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited.
The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services.

items.x: The other day I whizzed past several people while running in the park, my playlist blasting at full volume. The next morning, I smiled at a barista while ordering a caramel apple-flavored matcha latte. Afterward, I sat on a park bench reading a book, called up a pal to chat about her recent trip to Prague, and then asked my Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses what meetings were coming up on my calendar. The chipper AI voice said I hadn't connected my Google Calendar yet (I had) and asked if I would like help connecting. I sighed and then asked it to play an upbeat song. It picked Kendrick Lamar's "Not Like Us."

items.t: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
items.d: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.
items.x:
Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.
When I was eight, I remember our train to Mumbai ground to a halt with a great noise. When we started moving again, a good eight hours later, someone pointed out a mangled tail, of all things, hanging from a branch close to the tracks.
The train, you see, had apparently hit a wild bison at full speed, and the impact damaged the engine so badly that it had to be towed away for repairs. For a long time, I thought such things only happened in places like rural India, but I learned a few years ago that wildlife and infrastructure do not mix anywhere on the planet.
The FAA estimates that wildlife strikes have cost U.S. civil aviation about $272 million a year on average between 1990 and 2025. In France, the rail operator SNCF says wandering animals affect more than 8,000 trains across the country each year and are among its five leading causes of delays.

items.t: Disney offers $20M for Character.AI’s scandal-plagued chatbot tech
items.d: Disney may acquire tech from one of the first chatbot makers linked to child suicide.
items.x:
In a bankruptcy proceeding that kicked off yesterday, Disney has offered to buy some of the technology that powers the controversy-plagued chatbot Character.AI.
Disney is willing to pay $20 million for “a non-exclusive perpetual license” of certain Character Technologies intellectual property, the chatbot maker said in a press release that did not go into much further detail on what assets Disney wanted.
The move may be surprising. In September of 2025, Disney joined others in publicly criticizing Character.AI for stealing content and harming kids. Specifically, Disney sent a strongly worded cease-and-desist letter that accused Character Technologies of weaponizing Disney characters “in a way that could damage its brand long term,” Axios reported .

items.t: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
items.d: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.
items.x:
Facebook is the latest social media platform to give users greater control over the algorithm that determines what appears in their feeds. Meta
Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” on Tuesday, a feature it first launched on Instagram. The new tool allows Facebook users to influence the content they see in Feed and Reels by describing their preferences in their own words using natural language. Rather than relying entirely on automated recommendations, users can now communicate directly with the platform about the topics and content they want to see more or less frequently.
According to Meta, the feature is designed to make content recommendations more relevant. Users can adjust their preferences and interact with the algorithms responsible for ranking and recommending posts, with changes reflected in their recommendations in real time.
The company has also updated Facebook’s three-dot menu, making it easier for users to manage their content preferences directly from individual posts.

items.t: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
items.d: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least…
items.x:
Pluto Security has raised $42 million Jump Capital, TLV Partners, Ansa Capital and angel investors.
The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.
Illustrating the pace of AI tool adoption within enterprises driving such fears, Shahar Bahat, CEO and co-founder of Pluto Security, says a newly announced AI tool can show up inside companies’ environment within a mere two hours of its release. And about 60% of the risks her company detects across its customer base are in tools vibe-coded by non-developers: Finance departments are the biggest source of such risks, she told TechCrunch, followed by marketing and legal teams.

items.t: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
items.x:
How we built a reasoning agent with 2B active parameters Benchmark results Inference speed on CPU and GPU How to use LFM2.5-24B-A2B Use it in your agent harness Get Started with LFM2.5-24B-A2B Citation LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It thinks before it answers, calls tools, and works through multi-step tasks inside popular agent harnesses. Because only 2B parameters are active per token, each reasoning token is cheap, so you can run agents continuously on your own hardware.
![LFM2.5-24B-A2B-benchmark](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/resolve/main/figures/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-benchmark.png)
LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on LFM2-24B-A2B and keeps its architecture: 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and an in-place tokenizer expansion doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization. Unlike its predecessor, it is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer.
Pre-training was scaled up from ~17T to ~33T tokens.

Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
The Kenyan American engineer previously worked in Google’s cloud computing business before a brief stint at SpaceX’s Starlink communications network in 2024. His experiences convinced him that there was untapped potential for computers in space.
“When I was at SpaceX, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no. When I was at Google, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no,” he tells TechCrunch.
So he left SpaceX and co-founded Satlyt, a new company with headquarters in Sunnyvale, California, and Nairobi, to build software for satellites that he hopes will let many satellites share the work of large computing jobs in space. The company has raised an $8 million seed round, Afullo exclusively told TechCrunch.
The timing looks good for him. SpaceX has since gone all-in on orbital data centers, and Satlyt’s software is set to launch Thursday on a SpaceX rocket alongside the first prototype for Google’s space data center effort, Project Suncatcher.
Unlike SpaceX, Google, or startups like Starcloud and Cowboy Space Company, Satlyt isn’t planning to build its own spacecraft.

items.t: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
items.x:
Discover Gemini 4 Argon for robotics: leading the ERQA benchmark with physical reasoning, zero-shot control, Real2Sim, and agentic workflows.
Gemini 4 Argon marks a step change in physical understanding, code generation, and visual-semantic reasoning—unlocking new workflows across the robotics stack and accelerating progress toward physical AGI.
You can see this leap in capability on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, which tests a model's ability to understand and solve physical, spatial problems in 3D environments. Using pure reasoning, Argon scores 87%, outperforming every other frontier model.
As a general-purpose physical reasoning model, Argon can be applied across the entire robotics lifecycle. In this post, we share representative prompts for Argon across four key areas:
Argon controls a Boston Dynamics Spot® quadruped (12-DoF legs + 6-DoF arm) to learn a new skill: stepping on a foot-pedal trash bin to throw away soda cans. Argon creates an articulated MuJoCo digital twin of a foot-pedal trash bin to practice its moves before stepping on the physical pedal and dropping soda cans into the open bin.
Argon controls a simple robotic arm to place a fallen mug upright and put the crumpled napkin inside.

Google seems to have worked all that out pretty quickly, though. Argon is beginning its wide rollout today , but it's only coming to paying users at this time, and even those on lower-tier plans won't have full access.
Nothing about Gemini 4 Argon's capabilities has changed. Google still points to the benchmarks it published late last month as evidence of the model's advanced reasoning and agentic coding capabilities. The model has allegedly been carefully trained to refuse malicious instructions, and there's an automated misalignment monitor that can stop processing if it detects an unintended workflow. Google claims Argon needs that because it's so capable.
The company does have a few new examples of how Argon has helped inside Google, where it has been used by thousands of Googlers. items.t: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
items.d: Solar geoengineering simulation shows what happens when geopolitics takes over.
items.x:
When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. That was until one morning last September in London, when the climate researcher took part in the first in a series of war games. The goal: to prevent an uncontrolled global race to develop a technology aimed at cooling the planet but that comes with vast, unknown risks that could reshape life on Earth.
“I thought that would be such an easy thing. Like, we can all agree to do ethical research and make sure it's for the better of all humans,” she told WIRED. “And boy, was I wrong.”
The simulation, titled Exploring Geopolitical Tipping Points and Climate Cooling Strategies, saw a couple dozen foreign-relations experts, scientists, military personnel, and former government officials from across the world convene in a meeting room at Queen Mary University of London. After making introductions over coffee and little yogurts, they sat at tables arranged in a square with the name of the country or organization each person was playing: national governments, climate NGOs and nonprofits, indigenous groups, and tech companies. Golja was assigned to provide technical advice to help participants make scientifically literate decisions.

items.x:
American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.
Personal AI agents are increasingly making transactions on their users’ behalf, but given the nondeterministic nature of large language models, AI bots are prone to doing what they’re not supposed to. Which, in this case, raises the possibility of AI misfiring and making unauthorized transactions.
To get ahead of this problem, American Express is introducing a new framework designed to capture and authenticate a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes the transaction.
The idea is that there should be a way to ensure that the customer’s purchase instructions are carried throughout the transaction lifecycle, Amex says, from the purchase to everything that follows.
Dubbed the “Intent Intelligence Framework,” the company hopes it will become an industry standard for AI-powered transactions.
“These new transactions will have a consumer, a merchant, and an agent,” explained Amex’s VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy, Hannah Bozian, in an interview with TechCrunch.

items.t: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
items.d: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can
items.x:
Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk. The report’s core concern is that the powerful new model, released in August by the Chinese company Z.ai, is freely available for anyone to download and modify. Anthropic’s assertion is only the latest move in a long-running debate about whether frontier AI models should be made open, like GLM-5.3, or should stay locked behind the doors of the frontier labs.
These days, much of the debate about how to handle open models is playing out in public—and there’s a lot of money resting on its outcome. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has a lot to gain if people continue buying their own hardware to run open models, advocates enthusiastically for the United States to develop more of them, whereas Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, who runs a company that could be undermined by cheap, powerful models, advocates for a more cautious approach. But beneath all these commercial incentives, there is real substance to disagreements about open models.
“I think a lot of the way you come down on the openness debate is influenced by how you come down on the AI debate,” says David Gray Widder, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin School of Information.

items.t: AI Is Getting a Factory Job
items.d: Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart, a TechNode Group publication. The robot could follow the route. The worker knew when to skip it. Around 2022, Microintelligence encountered a problem that exposed the difference. A…
items.x:
Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart , a TechNode Group publication.
The robot could follow the route. The worker knew when to skip it.
Around 2022, Microintelligence encountered a problem that exposed the difference. A customer needed to inspect and grind a large die-cast component more than two metres long. The part required close to 3,000 imaging positions, and the customer wanted the process completed within ten minutes.
According to chairman and chief executive Zhang Zhiqi, a conventional robot following a fixed grinding path could take an hour. A skilled worker needed only seven or eight minutes.
The problem was not simply speed. A worker looked for imperfections and concentrated on the places that needed attention. The programmed machine followed its route.
For Microintelligence, the assignment pushed an inspection business toward a harder ambition: making what a machine sees determine what it does. Zhang described the project in a published interview; the customer was not identified, and the timing figures are his account rather than independently verified benchmarks. Interview with Zhang Zhiqi
That distinction—between finding a problem and acting on it—runs through the company’s development.

items.t: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.d: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money…
items.x:
When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says.
The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs.
SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April. Its Asset Hub platform helps founders sell their code and workspace data—emails, chats, documents. Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models.

items.t: Open-Source WeChatBridge Arrives on Windows in Beta, Sending WeChat Chats to Codex and Other Agents
items.d: WeChatBridge, a third-party open-source tool, now has a Windows beta that forwards selected WeChat chat records to AI agents such as Codex and Claude Code, or saves them to Obsidian.
items.x:
WeChatBridge, an open-source tool that forwards WeChat chat records to AI agents, has released a Windows version in beta. The project is built by independent developers and published on GitHub under the freestylefly account. It is not a Tencent product.
The tool fills a gap in WeChat's sharing menu. Newer versions of WeChat let users select several messages and forward them as a merged bundle to third-party apps, producing an archive with text, images and video. WeChatBridge adds entries to that forwarding menu so the bundle can go straight to coding and work agents such as Codex, Claude Code, WorkBuddy, Doubao and Qwen, or be saved as Markdown notes in Obsidian as a personal knowledge base.
The project launched for macOS at the end of September and has since passed about 1,200 stars on GitHub. Many users had asked for Windows support. The developers said the port took longer than expected because the Windows system architecture differs from macOS, and compatibility with older Windows builds required an extra layer. They said the feature works most smoothly on the latest Windows versions. The interface matches the Mac version.
The Windows release adds a way to collect more than 100 messages. WeChat normally shows a warning when a user tries to select over 100 records.

Buyers can sign in to Accio with their existing 1688 accounts. Sellers download a 1688 seller assistant inside Accio and link their store to start using it. Accio, which says it serves 10 million small and medium-sized businesses worldwide, focuses on the full e-commerce chain, from finding products and stocking up to closing orders, repeat purchases and store operations.
Most 1688 buyers are small businesses, many of them one-person operations, that source on 1688 and sell on Taobao, Tmall, Xiaohongshu, Pinduoduo, Douyin, cross-border marketplaces and instant retail. For them, Accio adds two main tools. A sourcing assistant covers both 1688 and Alibaba.com, letting buyers find suppliers, compare prices and send inquiries across 128 countries and regions. An e-commerce manager agent links Taobao, Tmall, Douyin, Pinduoduo and JD.com, so purchasing and store operations happen in one workspace.

According to IT Home and Leiphone, Qwen Go! can file flight-delay compensation claims, request price-protection refunds on Taobao, arrange car maintenance, book sports venues and compare prices across shops. When needed, it can query and operate the platforms a user has authorized, compare options and even phone service providers to finish a task.
Early testers have shared results. In one case described by Leiphone, a user simply asked Qwen Go! to get compensation from customer service. The agent checked the user's orders with four airlines to find the delayed flight, switched to online customer service when the hotline was blocked, declined a voucher in favor of cash, and secured a 70-yuan payout to the user's Alipay account. Another user said the agent noticed that a cookware item had dropped in price and claimed a 52-yuan price-protection refund.
Qwen has been positioned as a personal assistant that gets things done since it launched last year.

items.t: DeepSeek's Liang Wenfeng Is Meeting Embodied AI Founders as the Company Weighs a Move Into Robotics
items.d: DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng has been talking with embodied AI founders and is considering whether to build a team or enter the field another way, Phoenix Tech reports. DeepSeek has not responded.
items.x:
DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng has recently been paying close attention to embodied AI and has held conversations with a number of founders in the field, Phoenix Tech reported on October 12. The discussions covered robotics, large models and how AI systems interact with the physical world.
According to people familiar with the matter cited in the report, Liang is considering whether DeepSeek should move further into embodied AI. Two routes are said to be under discussion: assembling an in-house team to do the research and development directly, or entering the field through stakes in companies already working on it. No decision has been reported.
One person told Phoenix Tech that Liang does not have much experience in the field and has been studying it intensively. DeepSeek had not responded to requests for comment as of publication, Sina Tech noted.
The report linked part of the interest to recent progress elsewhere. It said several test demos have shown OpenAI's GPT-6 achieving execution results on embodied tasks that surprised the industry, and suggested that this is one of the pressures behind DeepSeek's thinking.
Another industry figure quoted in the coverage said a move would not be surprising.

items.t: ByteDance’s Seed AI lab creates dedicated model safety and alignment department

items.x:
ByteDance’s Seed AI lab is establishing a dedicated Model-Alignment & Preparedness department, according to an internal email reported by The Paper on October 13. Yan Lin will lead the unit and report to Seed head Wu Yonghui. Members of the existing Responsible AI team and some employees from the Chat team will transfer to the new department.
The unit will develop model-behavior specifications, safety evaluations, alignment training, protective systems and risk monitoring. Its remit includes improving AI agents’ ability to operate within human intentions and authorized limits, as well as addressing chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks associated with advanced models.
Seed also plans to expand public cooperation with external researchers and independent evaluators. The move creates a separate organizational home for safety and alignment work as the lab develops increasingly capable and autonomous AI systems. [ The Paper , in Chinese]

items.t: Alibaba prepares Qwen Go personal AI assistant for claims, bookings and shopping

items.x:
Alibaba is preparing to introduce Qwen Go, a personal AI assistant that can handle tasks such as flight-delay compensation claims, shopping refunds, car-servicing appointments and sports-venue bookings. Reports on October 13 described trials in which the assistant accessed services, compared options and contacted customer support on users’ behalf.
In one shared demonstration, Qwen Go checked a user’s flight history, identified an eligible delay and negotiated RMB 70 in cash compensation after a phone call failed and it switched to text-based customer support. Its actions were visible on screen, and the user could intervene or stop the process. The upgrade builds on Qwen’s existing connections to Alibaba services for shopping, transport and deliveries. [ National Business Daily , in Chinese]

items.t: China's Rail Tech Plan for 2026-2030 Targets 400 km/h CR450 Service and 600 km/h Maglev Testing
items.d: The National Railway Administration's 2026-2030 railway tech plan covers CR450 trains for 400 km/h service, 600 km/h maglev test validation, an AI upgrade for 12306 and 5G-R networks.
items.x:
China's National Railway Administration has issued its railway science and technology innovation plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, covering 2026 to 2030. Published on October 12, the plan sets out research priorities ranging from faster trains and more automated construction to artificial intelligence across ticketing, freight and maintenance.
Its most visible goal concerns speed. The plan calls for basic research on wheel-rail wear, pantograph and catenary interaction and signaling at 400 km/h, and for a low-drag, low-noise, low-axle-load design suited to batch operation at that speed, producing a CR450 family of trains. A maintenance and overhaul system for 400 km/h trains is also on the list.
On maglev, the wording is careful. The administration says it will steadily and in an orderly way advance research on 600 km/h high-speed maglev technology and test validation of key technologies for domestic production. The plan describes research and testing rather than construction of a line.
Passenger service is another focus. The plan calls for upgrading the 12306 platform from a ticketing tool into an intelligent service that covers an entire journey, with personalized multimodal trip planning.

items.t: Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI
items.d: Uber's CISO, Philip Martin, on the importance of monitoring and observability for AI agents, and how Uber's open-source tooling works alongside Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.
items.x:
The importance of monitoring and observability for AI agents, and how Uber's open-source tooling works alongside Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.
Uber's CISO, Philip Martin, on the importance of monitoring and observability for AI agents, and how Uber's open-source tooling works alongside Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.
Uber runs one of the world's largest real-time marketplaces, with over 40 million trips and delivery orders a day. Philip Martin, Uber's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), leads the team that protects Uber's data and the riders, drivers, and couriers who use the platform in the real world. His team started working with Claude on threat modeling before Claude Code existed, assembling context by hand. Now, with Claude Fable, Claude gathers that context itself from code, design docs, and ticket history.
Martin thinks AI agents need the same kind of insider threat program companies already run for their employees.
