أطلقت شركة ميتا نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الجديد Muse Wonder، بهدف تطوير مساعدين رقميين قادرين على تذكّر المعلومات الشخصية للمستخدمين عبر المحادثات الممتدة لأسابيع أو أشهر، بالإضافة إلى تنفيذ المهام اليومية والمهنية دون الحاجة إلى توجيهات مستمرة.
ويأتي النموذج ضمن توجه ميتا نحو تطوير وكلاء ذكاء اصطناعي أكثر استقلالية، يمكنهم التعامل مع المهام المعقدة والتكيف مع المشكلات التي تواجههم في أثناء التنفيذ، بدلًا من الاكتفاء بالإجابة عن الأسئلة أو إنشاء المحتوى.
وطوّرت ميتا النموذج ضمن مختبر Superintelligence Lab، الذي يقوده ألكسندر وانغ، وقد درّبته في مركز بيانات Prometheus التابع للشركة في ولاية أوهايو الأمريكية.
ويشكّل Muse Wonder أول إطلاق لنموذج متقدم من هذه الفئة لدى ميتا منذ أكثر من عام، وتضم السلسلة الجديدة نموذجين هما Muse Wonder، وMuse Wonder Full الموجّه إلى المطورين.
وركّزت الشركة على المهام الشخصية والمهنية اليومية، مثل تحليل السجلات المالية المعقدة، ومراجعة عقود الإيجار، وتنظيم جداول المواعيد المزدحمة، بدلًا من حصر قدرات النماذج في كتابة الأكواد البرمجية.
ويعتمد النموذج على ميزتين رئيسيتين هما “الذاكرة النشطة Active Memory” و”التركيز النشط Active Focus”.

items.t: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
items.d: "No more hand-written code" or AI-free art for delayed Marvel/Star Wars shooter.
items.x:
Epic Games is shifting to an "AI first" development strategy for its collaboration with the Walt Disney Company, letting AI models write all the code and guide all the artwork for an upcoming shooter. That's according to a Bloomberg report , which cites unnamed people familiar with the project who commented on the significant pivot in internal development at the Unreal Engine maker.
Human developers will be tasked with managing and guiding code and art assets generated by models such as Anthropic's Claude, according to internal Epic employee messages viewed by Bloomberg. That means "no more hand-written code" and art assets "generated with full AI workflows," according to the report.
The $1.5 billion collaboration between Epic and Disney, announced in early 2024 , was slated to release a Marvel- and Star Wars-themed shooter in March 2027. That project has now been delayed indefinitely amid the AI-related shakeup and understaffed, slower-than-expected development thus far, according to the report.

items.t: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
items.d: “I may have information regarding this case," Claude AI told Philly police.
items.x:
An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, the company and police department confirmed on Friday.
A Claude model sent the false tip on July 18 to the Philadelphia Police Department's website for submitting information about unsolved murders, but it was flagged by a spam filter. Anthropic apparently discovered the incident on September 28 and informed the police department about it on October 8.
During internal testing, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete various forms up to the final submission stage and to stop before submitting those forms. "Several times Claude mistakenly submitted the form instead, expecting there to be an additional confirmation page," Anthropic said in a report describing "unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude."

items.t: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
items.d: Russian bloggers warn Russia’s hyper-centralized digital economy is vulnerable.
items.x:
When Russia began attacking Ukrainian data centers and telecommunication infrastructure, it apparently failed to prepare for possible retaliation. Now Russia’s digital services are facing widespread outages after Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out three of the largest data centers owned by Russian tech giant Yandex within several days.
Pro-Kremlin bloggers are warning that Russia’s centralized digital economy could collapse, because the country is not prepared for the “data center war” it started, according to posts translated by the pseudonymous independent researcher ChrisO_wiki . The Russian commentators also suggested that Ukraine’s decentralized digital services could prove more resilient than Russia’s system if the countries continue trading such blows.
Russia initially launched a drone strike campaign targeting Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in late September. The attacks temporarily disrupted Internet and cell phone service for up to 100,000 households in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and came as part of a broader long-range strike campaign that has involved Russian missiles and jet-powered drones hitting Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, transportation hubs, and even residential apartment building blocks.

items.t: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
items.d: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.
items.x:
A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a US military contract worth almost $50 million.
The U.S. Air Force will buy data collected by WindBorne Systems‘ fleet of autonomous weather balloons under a new contract that could be worth nearly $50 million to the startup.
WindBorne currently has about 700 weather balloons flying around the globe, collecting atmospheric sensor readings that the company sells to customers and also feeds into its own AI weather forecasting model. WindBorne, founded in 2015 and based in Redwood City, Calif., is one of the first organizations to directly feed empirical data into a deep-learning weather model.
The company has worked closely with the U.S. government, particularly the National Weather Service and the U.S. Air Force and Navy, but this is the single largest contract the company has participated in. The contract is worth up to $49 million, but the Air Force pays only as it needs data. It can place orders for specific regions at specific times.

items.x:
Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?
Honeyjar, which will be attending this week’s TechCrunch Disrupt as part of the Startup Battlefield 200, wants to use AI to make the expertise and judgment of the best PR pros available to everyone, including founders who have no idea where to start.
The startup’s founders, CEO Michelle Masek and CCO Nadia Jamshidi, certainly fit the bill when it comes to PR expertise. They’ve both spent decades in the field, doing in-house communications and working at agencies. Masek recently served as senior vice president of marketing and communications for Ev Williams’ venture firm, Obvious Ventures.
As Masek described the challenges involved in “helping with the why and when of comms and marketing for 110 portfolio companies” (the startups her firm had invested in), I flashed back to my own brief stint leading marketing at an early-stage VC firm, where founders were constantly asking for help getting into TechCrunch.

items.t: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation

Microsoft President Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.
Microsoft President Brad Smith is calling for urgent regulation of AI, and his argument is that consumer products like milk and washing machines have more oversight than the companies building artificial intelligence.
On a recent BBC podcast, Smith called AI both a “weapon and a tool” that is putting the world’s cybersecurity at risk, and said the “moment has arrived” to institute global safety rules.
Smith also said the U.K., and not the U.S. or European Union, is best placed to lead on global safety rules. Britain’s AI Security Institute, launched in 2023, receives access to major models from U.S. frontier labs before they are deployed and has quickly become a leader in AI safety testing.

items.x:
Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.
Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Drams was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him.
There was just one problem: the technology his idea required didn’t exist yet.
“Then ChatGPT came along,” said Drams, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022.
His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF.
Blueprints AI, which Drams officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200, a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

تستعد شركة ميتا لإضافة ميزة جدولة الرسائل إلى تطبيق واتساب، بما يتيح للمستخدمين تحديد موعد إرسال الرسائل بنحو مسبق، سواء لتعيين التذكيرات المتكررة أو مراعاة فروق التوقيت أو تنظيم التواصل في أوقات خارج ساعات العمل.
وظهرت الميزة الجديدة في الإصدار التجريبي من تطبيق واتساب لنظام أندرويد، الذي يحمل الرقم 2.26.8.11، وفقًا لموقع “WaBetaInfo” المتخصص في متابعة تحديثات التطبيق، في خطوة تمهّد لإتاحتها للمستخدمين خلال الآونة المقبلة.
وتتيح الميزة للمستخدمين جدولة الرسائل عبر الضغط المطول على زر الإرسال، لتظهر نافذة تسمح بتحديد التاريخ والوقت المناسبين لإرسال الرسالة. كما توفر قسمًا مخصصًا لإدارة الرسائل المجدولة ومراجعتها قبل موعد إرسالها.
ويمكن إرسال الرسائل المجدولة حتى في حال عدم اتصال الهاتف بالإنترنت وقت الإرسال، على أن تدعم الميزة النصوص والروابط والصور ومقاطع الفيديو، بالإضافة إلى المحادثات الجماعية.
ووفقًا للمعلومات المتاحة، فإن المستخدم يستطيع تحديد موعد الإرسال قبل 10 دقائق على الأقل من الوقت الحالي، أو تأجيله لمدة تصل إلى أسبوعين.

items.t: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background
items.d: One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you'll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to…
items.x:
Ambi is releasing apps for iPhone, Mac, and Apple Watch that enables ambient capture
One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you’ll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to listen, watch or record users’ activity all the time and gather all possible context.
There’s obviously privacy and data security concerns with anything that’s collecting data about you continuously. But startups are building such apps undeterred anyway, arming themselves with the belief that the market for personalized assistance is big enough to swallow such concerns.
Former Plaud exec Peter Mo is building Ambi to do something similar. The app aims to provide real-time intelligence and insights to people by listening to them all the time.
The company said on Monday that it has raised $26 million across multiple funding rounds led by Luminous Ventures, which has backed companies like Meituan and Unitree Robotics, and Original Design Manufacturer (ODM) Huaqin.
Ambi is also releasing apps for iPhones, Macs and Apple Watch.

items.t: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
items.d: The second-largest corporate employer has bet big on robot workers to scale.
items.x:
No organization in the world operates more robots than Amazon. The company already has more than 1 million robots working in warehouses around the clock to make tens of millions of same-day and one-day package deliveries happen on a daily basis—and Amazon is poised to significantly grow that robotic fleet in the coming years as it establishes new factories to churn out increasingly more capable robot workers.
Despite deploying so many robots, Amazon is also the second-largest corporate employer in the world, with more than 1.5 million full-time and part-time human workers, according to its 2025 annual report . Amazon executives say that the growing robot fleet has eased the burden on its human workforce by taking on the toughest fulfillment center tasks that carry the greatest risks of physical fatigue and injury.

items.t: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
items.d: Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it's now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the…
items.x:
Meta says the models compete with the industry’s best and will soon power its Muse agent.
Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it’s now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the industry’s best.
The company says its new models can rival leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1, pointing to results from internal testing on several industry benchmarks. It’s unclear how they stack up against Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, whose capabilities are still coming into focus.
The launches are part of Meta’s aggressive push to reestablish itself as a major force in AI. The company has poured billions into talent and infrastructure and has been steadily expanding its AI lineup, including with image model Muse Image and a heavy focus on bringing useful AI agents to the masses through Muse.
